extracted.intended_audience: federal, state, or regulatory lobbyists and government relations professionals seeking a professional certificate
extracted.subtask_description: Program requirements and policies for the Public Affairs Council's Certificate in Government Relations and Lobbying, including eligibility, credit/attendance rules, credit-breakdown by category, community-credit options, and administrative/cost details. Intended to guide applicants and enrolled participants on how to earn the certificate within program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility - minimum experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must have a minimum of two years of experience in a position related to government relations, advocacy, public affairs, or one full year serving as a legislative or agency staffer at the federal or state level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prerequisite to enroll; applicants who do not meet these experience thresholds are not eligible. Programs attended up to one month prior to the application date will be counted toward the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe to complete certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should complete the program requirements within three years of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate allows three years to meet all requirements, though many graduate sooner. Participants are expected to meet all credit and attendance requirements within that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total credit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate completion requires 25 credits split among several credit areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must accumulate a total of 25 credits according to the specified category breakdown (see specialized categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying/Government Relations Specialization credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Lobbying or Government Relations Specialization: 16 credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earn these credits by participating in webinars and workshops on government relations and by attending The Advocacy Conference or the Government Relations & Policy Conference. Credit must come from eligible (PAC) programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Management credits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend compliance programs to build expertise in legal rules and ethics; these programs count toward the 4 compliance-management credits required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Engagement credits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earn these by engaging with peers (posting on Council Connect), providing or creating resources, speaking at or helping plan events, or other community activities described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory conference attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must attend either The Advocacy Conference or the Government Relations & Policy Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance at one of these named PAC conferences is a program requirement. NOTE: Credit cannot be earned through attendance at non-Public Affairs Council programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live participation requirement (no recordings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registered participation in live webinars is eligible for certificate credit. Purchase of webinar recordings is not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attending a recorded webinar after the fact does not earn credit; you must be a registered live participant for the event in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual attendance logging rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Earning credit as a virtual participant requires logging onto Zoom, or the virtual workshop platform, with your name, job title and organization for the duration of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration without attendance or early departure from an event will not count toward certificate completion. Participants are encouraged to provide feedback and commentary during discussion periods to demonstrate engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - posting on Council Connect
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting on Council Connect — 1 credit for each five posts of substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'substance': starting a thread, commenting in a way that forwards the conversation or shares insight, or sharing professional expertise that assists colleagues. Platform is only available to Public Affairs Council members. Credit achievement is subject to Council staff discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - resource submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting government relations- and/or lobbying-related resources to be shared in the Council’s resource library — 1 credit per five resources submitted, up to a maximum of 2 credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be relevant resources. Credits for submitted resources are capped at 2 credits total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - speaking at Council programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving as a speaker at a Council program (at the discretion of Council staff) — 2 credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speaker participation is awarded credits when approved by Council staff; speaking roles are evaluated at staff discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - conference advisory committee service
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving as an active member of a Conference Advisory Committee — 1 credit (awarded after the relevant conference occurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active members participate in advisory committee meetings and calls or connect with staff to submit suggestions, market and promote the conference, and support conference success through active participation. Credit awarded post-conference and at staff discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - authored web content
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing an article or tip sheet for use on the Council’s website or in a newsletter (in collaboration with Council staff) — 2 credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be produced in collaboration with Council staff and meet editorial/use criteria to qualify for credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community credits - discretionary approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Community credits may be earned for specified activities, but achievement of these credits is subject to the discretion of Council staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an activity matches listed examples, Council staff evaluate and approve credit awards; do not assume automatic credit without staff confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs timing that count toward application
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs attended up to one month prior to the application date will be counted toward the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you attended eligible programs within the 1-month window before applying, those programs may be applied to your credit total for the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirement for some credit activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain community-credit activities (e.g., posting on Council Connect) are only available to Public Affairs Council members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-members cannot access Council Connect to earn posting-based community credits; membership or equivalent access is required for those credit types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative application fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A $199 administrative fee will be applied to all applications accepted on or after October 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fee is charged upon acceptance of the application; contact [email protected] for questions about cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program cost range and membership discount
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate cost can vary depending on program choices and membership status, but typically ranges from $4,000 – $5,400. Membership Plus+ can substantively reduce program costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs depend on which eligible programs a participant attends and whether they are a Council member; consult the cost comparison link or contact the Council for specific pricing.
